results.summary_before: This project generates a 640x480 VGA display with moving color tiles. It outputs RGB222 video signals along with HSync and VSync, and is intended to be used with a Tiny VGA PMOD connected to a VGA monitor. Testing requires applying power and releasing reset after connecting the PMOD and monitor. The design is a straightforward demonstration of VGA output on the Tiny Tapeout platform, with no additional processing or external interfaces beyond the VGA connection.

results.summary_before: This project is a digital simulation of two qubits and an entangled pair, imitating quantum behaviour with registers, comparators, and three maximal-length LFSRs for probabilistic collapse. It is controlled by four input switches for initial states, Hadamard gate application, and measurement, with four LED outputs displaying the results. The design was prototyped in Wokwi and uses a 100 Hz clock, making it suitable for educational demonstrations. It does not perform real quantum computation and the randomness is a simplified stand-in based on LFSRs.

results.summary_before: This analog block implements an 8-bit R2R digital-to-analog converter with a 3.3 V output achieved through level-shifting drivers. It can be driven externally via the digital input pins or by an internal digital sine waveform generator, with control pins for loading and an external data input. An oscilloscope is required to measure the analog output voltage on the dedicated analog pin. The design is straightforward and no detailed performance specifications are provided.

results.summary_before: This design is a Pong game with retro visuals and an AI opponent, forked from an earlier version. It supports both two-player and AI modes, selectable via a DIP switch, and uses a VGA display and Pmod game controllers for input. The game includes serve and paddle controls for each player. Testing involves pressing the select button to serve and flipping the DIP switch to change modes.

results.summary_before: Poket Animal is a tamagotchi-style virtual pet that lives on a 7-segment display, tracking hunger, joy, sickness and death with distinct display moods and animations. Two debounced buttons feed and pet the creature, while status pins report alive, heartbeat, cause of death, sickness, hunger level and wiggle, and a two-bit speed selector sets the metabolic tick rate from about 1.9 hours down to simulation speed. Overfeeding causes indigestion and eventually death, starvation kills after two ticks, and death is sticky until reset. It needs a common-cathode 7-segment display with decimal point, two push buttons and optionally an LED for the heartbeat, and the cocotb testbench exercises the full lifecycle in turbo mode.

results.summary_before: This project implements a whac-a-mole style game called 'Catch the fish', using a 6-bit Fibonacci LFSR and a simple timer to generate pseudo-random outputs. Players press one of three buttons when the corresponding feedback output is high to score, with a reward feedback provided. It requires a clock and three buttons, and outputs feedback signals. It is designed for the Wokwi simulator and is a game; no silicon test results are reported.
